Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the StratoCloud Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an option to withdraw your question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing StratoCloud's results for the third quarter of 2024. With me on the call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Mike Thornton, Chief Product Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. StratoCloud delivered another strong Q3, marked by significant growth in our core cloud business and increasing adoption of our innovative AI solutions.

During the quarter, our priorities were focused on six key areas:
1. Expanding our global cloud infrastructure footprint.
2. Driving innovation in serverless computing.
3. Enhancing our cybersecurity offerings.
4. Strengthening our partnerships with leading ISVs.
5. Improving customer satisfaction and retention.
6. Investing in our talent pool and fostering a culture of innovation.

I'm particularly thrilled to highlight one of the most transformative drivers behind our results: the explosive growth in AI and machine learning workloads. StratoCloud has positioned itself at the forefront of the cloud computing revolution, powering over 150,000 enterprise customers worldwide with our scalable infrastructure, including our flagship StratoAI Platform and next-generation accelerators. In Q3, we saw a 62% year-over-year surge in compute hours dedicated to AI/ML workloads across our global regions. This encompasses both training and inference, with inference workloads—which now make up 68% of total AI/ML compute—growing even faster at 71% year-over-year. Training workloads expanded by 52% year-over-year, propelled by fine-tuning and transfer learning applications.

Adoption rates are equally compelling: the number of active AI/ML customers on our platform rose 58% to more than 45,000, while enterprise adoption—customers running workloads over 1 petaFLOP—increased by 65%. Even small and medium businesses saw a 49% uptick, thanks to our pay-as-you-go Strato ML Studio that eases entry for prototyping large language models.

This momentum stems from the generative AI boom sparked by models like GPT-4 and Llama 2, pushing enterprises from proofs-of-concept to production. We've noted a threefold rise in retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, integrating our Strato VectorSearch with foundation models for real-time search and chatbots. Multimodal AI workloads blending vision, language, and audio surged 89% quarter-over-quarter, as seen in media and autonomous systems fine-tuning models like CLIP variants on our GPU clusters.

Technically, our launches are delivering results. The Strato XA-300 AI Accelerator—our third-generation custom silicon for sparse matrix operations—has grabbed 22% market share in new AI training clusters, outperforming NVIDIA H100 and AMD MI300X with up to 4 petaFLOPS of FP8 performance per node at 40% lower total cost of ownership, powered by tensor parallelism and ZeRO-Offload in our Strato ML Runtime. Our ModelForge service, akin to Bedrock, supports over 100 pre-trained models from Meta, Anthropic, and Stability AI with Kubernetes-native auto-scaling. The Inference Optimization Service employs dynamic graph pruning and quantization to cut latency by 55% for trillion-parameter models, with early adopters like a top global bank achieving 3x throughput on RAG workloads.

Regionally, North America leads with 52% of AI/ML revenue and 55% growth, driven by hyperscalers and financial giants migrating to our sovereign zones. EMEA grew 49%, aided by GDPR-compliant federated learning and automotive updates via Strato Autonomous Edge. APAC exploded 72%, with China ramping e-commerce engines through Alibaba partnerships and Southeast Asia spiking post-Bangkok and Singapore expansions for telcos like Singtel.

We're investing $4.5 billion from record free cash flow into AI capex, adding 50,000 XA-300 nodes and exploring quantum-hybrid ML. Our AI runs on 85% renewables, cutting carbon intensity 28% with liquid cooling. Our net promoter score for AI services is 78, beating peers, thanks to hybrid bursting via Strato Fabric.

Forward-looking, we anticipate 50-55% AI/ML revenue growth in Q4, with workloads up 65% annually as inference margins hit 72%. Supply chain risks persist, but diversified partnerships protect us. AI/ML is redefining compute, and StratoCloud is the backbone.

Now I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to provide a detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q3. Revenue increased by 32% year-over-year to $3.2 billion, driven by strong demand for our cloud services. Our gross margin was 68%, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency. Our operating margin was 25%.

Before we move on, let me dive deeper into one of our most critical forward-looking metrics: Remaining Performance Obligations, or RPO. RPO offers the clearest view into our revenue visibility, capturing committed value from customer contracts not yet recognized under ASC 606, emphasizing multi-year subscriptions central to our model.

Headline numbers show durability: Total RPO ended Q3 at $47.2 billion, up 38% year-over-year—our strongest in over two years, exceeding our 32-35% guide. Current RPO, for recognition within 12 months, hit $23.8 billion, up 42% year-over-year, with 82% of total RPO now current versus 78% last year, boosting FY25 visibility. Non-current RPO reached $23.4 billion, up 35%, highlighting multi-year enterprise deals with average contract values over $50 million for top customers.

Contextualizing, dollar-based net retention rate hit 128%, with 115% gross retention and expansions into generative AI inference and LLM fine-tuning. A major U.S. financial firm expanded StratoCloud Kubernetes clusters threefold for fraud detection using Strato VectorForge database with NVIDIA H100s via StratoAI.

Driving factors: AI bookings at 45% of RPO additions, up from 32%, with StratoAI Bedrock-compatible hosting—40% lower latency than AWS SageMaker—securing a $1.2 billion, five-year deal from a European automotive OEM for autonomous simulations. AI/ML RPO alone grew 62% to $12.5 billion.

Cloud-native modernization added tailwinds, converting 25% more mainframe workloads to StratoShift with eBPF observability, lifting core compute/storage RPO 29%. 

Regionally: Americas $28.1 billion (60%), up 41%, via FedRAMP High Virginia region ($800 million committed). EMEA $11.4 billion (24%), up 52% with GDPR zones in Frankfurt/Paris, including Siemens Industry 4.0 ($900 million). APAC $7.7 billion (16%), up 28% QoQ to 35%, with Tokyo/Sydney expansions and a $600 million Japanese telco 5G deal.

Our land-and-expand flywheel thrives with 36-month average contracts bundling IaaS/PaaS, StratoQuantum, and CarbonNeutral credits; 92% of additions from NRR >110% customers. Q4 RPO growth guided 35-40%, backing FY25 revenue $12.8-13.2 billion (28% midpoint), 90-95% cRPO conversion. Outpacing peers like Snowflake's 34%, next up: GaiaOS for 25% TCO cuts.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. On the technology front, we made significant progress in several areas. We successfully launched our next-generation StratoCompute platform, which offers enhanced performance and scalability.

As we discuss our advancements, I want to emphasize our heightened investments in security infrastructure and personnel—one of our top priorities in a landscape where trust differentiates us from hyperscalers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud for enterprise-scale workloads. In Q3, we committed $185 million to security CapEx and OpEx, up 28% year-over-year and 14% of total R&D. Full-year 2024 guidance is $750 million, a 32% rise from $567 million last year—60% to infrastructure like hardware and data center hardening, 40% to personnel.

Our global security team grew to 1,450 full-time equivalents, up 22%, with 320 Q3 hires in threat hunting, incident response, and DevSecOps at $285,000 average compensation, bolstered by equity to combat 15-20% attrition. Our Security Academy, with $12 million invested, upskills 80% of engineers on zero-trust and AI anomaly detection, slashing mean time to detect to under 12 hours from 48.

Infrastructure-wise, $120 million rolled out confidential computing in 28 regions using Intel SGX and AMD SEV-SNP for encrypted in-use workloads, spurring 35% growth in HIPAA/PCI-DSS migrations. Our StratoShield platform, with homomorphic encryption from IBM and Duality, analyzes 2.5 petabytes daily across 15,000 VPCs, cutting false positives 40% below Gartner's 65% benchmark. We're advancing quantum-resistant crypto like CRYSTALS-Kyber against future threats.

Regionally tailored: EMEA ($41 million, 22%) meets NIS2/Schrems II for €2.5 billion sovereign deals. APAC ($38 million) features air-gapped regions for PDPA compliance at 99.999% uptime. Americas ($83 million, 45%) advances FedRAMP High for DoD IL5/IL6.

ROI is evident: 18% QoQ NRR to 128%, security topping NPS criteria. Q3 closed 15 $100M+ deals, like $450 million bank contract for zero-trust SASE and 50ms threat SLA. These fuel 25-30% high-margin growth, outpacing IDC's 22% IaaS CAGR. Upcoming: Quantum Forge at re:Invent.

Now, I'll pass it over to Mike Thornton for a product roadmap update.

Mike Thornton:
Thank you, Elena. We are excited about the market reception to our new StratoAI offering. This product is designed to address the evolving needs of our customers in the enterprise sector.

Today, I'd like to explore our Average Revenue Per User—or ARPU—metrics, a key measure of our wallet share expansion in cloud. We calculate ARPU as trailing twelve-month cloud revenue divided by active accounts, tracking upsell to AI/ML, analytics, and hybrid solutions.

Q3 ARPU hit $48,200, up 17% year-over-year from $41,300 and 4% sequentially, accelerating from Q1's 12% amid AI momentum and NexGen AI Suite wins.

By segment: Enterprise (> $1M TTM, 28% accounts/72% revenue) ARPU $285,000, +22%, from sovereign migrations and AI inference; top 500 up 28%. Mid-market ($100K-$1M) $42,500, +14%, via self-service console. SMB/startups (<$100K, 65% accounts) $6,800, +11%, with serverless upsell.

By category: Compute/Storage $18,400 (38%), +12% (Graviton4, NexEdge); AI/ML/GenAI $12,600 (26%), +42% (Strato AI Studio, TrainX); Databases/Analytics $9,200 (19%), +18%; Networking/Security $5,500 (11%), +15%; SaaS/Other $2,500 (6%), +8%.

Driven by StratoGen AI Suite bundling (35% attach), sustainable cloud, and AWS/Azure interoperability ($200M hybrid). Regionally: Americas $52,100 (+16%), EMEA $46,800 (+20% GDPR), APAC $40,200 (+19% hyperscale).

Outlook: $52,000-$54,000 FY24 end (15-18% growth) via AI monetization ($4K lift), 3.2 services cross-sell, 5-7% pricing. This cements partnerships with sticky workloads.

I'll now hand it over to Lisa Patel to discuss our marketing initiatives.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Mike. We have been focused on driving brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly effective in reaching our target audience.

A key element in our global strategy is navigating the impact of currency fluctuations on revenue, given over 45% international exposure in our $3.2 billion Q3 top line. FX headwinds trimmed 250 basis points from reported growth, but constant currency shows 30.5% versus 28% reported; year-to-date, 2.8 point drag.

Americas (55%, $1.76B): $45M BRL hit (1.1%), offset by São Paulo sovereign. EMEA (25%, $800M): $120M euro/sterling drag (4.2% reported vs. 38% constant), UK SaaS volatility. APAC (15%, $480M): $65M JPY weakness (1.9%), AUD stable, India +55%. Rest ($160M): minor lira impact.

USD +4.5% drove this. Mitigation: 75% hedged ($180M gains), 65% local billing (40% volatility cut), dynamic pricing (3-5% EUR/JPY uplift, ASP $0.045/GB-month stable). Tech: multi-region replication, 52% long commitments.

RPO $47.2B grew 42%, minimally FX-hit. Diversifying to INR/MXN, USD AI, Jakarta Q1 launch. Q4: 27-29% reported, 30-32% constant.

Back to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Lisa. We are confident that our strong financial performance, innovative technology, and talented team will enable us to continue to deliver exceptional value to our customers and shareholders.

Wrapping up on our overall gross margin trends, a focus for profitability in this competitive space. Q3 consolidated gross margin reached 68.2%, up 320 basis points year-over-year from 65.0% and 110 sequentially—11th straight expansion quarter, above 65-70% target. Non-GAAP 69.5%, topping AWS 69%, Azure 68%, Google 64%.

Revenue mix drove 150 bps: platform/software (StratoML, StratoAI) 42% mix (from 35%), 82% margins; IaaS 48% at 62%; edge/sovereign 10% at 55%. Efficiencies added 200 bps: 87% utilization (predictive orchestration), PUE 1.10 (liquid cooling, 30% renewables), 8% lower depreciation. StratoCore ARM powers 65% inference (40% TOPS/watt savings), TSMC deals stabilize supply.

Regional: Americas 71% (Magnificent Seven AI), EMEA 67% (GDPR costs), APAC 64% (expansions). Headwinds: 2% pricing compression, 30 bps FX, 100 bps AI capacity—manageable.

Q4 guide 68.5-69.0%, FY 69.5% via 25% AI mix, PUE <1.05 centers, Azure Stack partnerships, AIOps 10% COGS cut. Risks: GPUs, EU energy—diversified stack protects.

This scale-to-efficiency positions us in $600B TAM.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Thanks for taking my question. Jordan or Sarah, the RPO growth was impressive at 38%, especially the AI contribution. Can you speak more to the sustainability of that acceleration and how it factors into FY25 guidance?

Jordan Hale:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, the 38% RPO print reflects durable demand, with AI at 45% of additions and 62% growth in that bucket alone. Sustainability comes from multi-year deals like the $1.2B automotive commitment and our land-and-expand with 128% NRR. We're guiding 35-40% into Q4, supporting the raised FY25 revenue midpoint of about 28% growth, with high conversion rates. Sarah?

Sarah Chen:
Yes, Ben, our 92% high-NRR additions and shift to 36-month contracts enhance quality. No macro shocks assumed, but our balanced regions and modernization tailwinds position us well ahead of peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Laura Kim:
Great, thanks. Elena, on the security investments ramping to $750 million this year, what's the expected payback period and how it's influencing win rates in regulated verticals?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Laura. Payback is strong—already driving 18% NRR lift and 15 $100M+ deals in Q3, like the $450M bank win citing our SASE and SLAs. Enterprise NPS ranks security #1, with ROI via 25-30% segment growth. Personnel cuts MTTD sharply, infrastructure like confidential computing boosts regulated migrations 35%. Expect full-year returns as utilization hits, mirroring IDC forecasts.

Sarah Chen:
To add, these are high-margin expansions, supporting our 68%+ gross margins.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are committed to transparency and open communication with our investors.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
